title: Marketplace partner intake: mini-audit and copy playbook
body:
Context and goal:
This is a compact intake + audit doc to help partner managers and engineers run a fast acceptance check for new cloud marketplace listings (public tiles, cloud-shelf, private offers). Purpose: align on minimal launch-ready requirements, provide ready-to-paste microcopy variants, and surface early legal/engineering blockers so we can run a 72-hr acceptance sprint for low-risk partners.

Who should use this:
- Partner PM / GTM owner (owns partner communication and copy)
- Integration engineer (verifies technical requirements)
- Security/compliance reviewer (quick gate)
- Listing ops (publishes tile)

Quick intake summary (complete during first call):
- Partner name: <partner-org>
- Primary contact: <name, email, slack>
- Target offering: hosted API integration / connector / managed private deployment
- Tier: SMB / Mid-market / Enterprise
- Required go-live date (if any): <date>
- Estimated complexity: low / medium / high

Mini-audit checklist (green = must pass before tile copy goes to design):
1) Product fit & SKU mapping (owner: GTM) [PASS/FAIL]
   - Short description for customers (<= 20 words) provided by partner or draftable by us
   - SKU mapping: trial SKU + paid SKU + entitlements documented
   - Billing model compatible with marketplace (metering, trial, subscription)
2) Asset readiness (owner: listing ops) [PASS/FAIL]
   - 1 hero image (16:9) and 3 thumbnails (icons / screenshots)
   - 30–60s video demo (optional), or 3 annotated screenshots
   - Logo (SVG + PNG 512px) and short company blurb (<= 50 words)
3) Copy and messaging (owner: GTM) [PASS/FAIL]
   - 2-line hero headline (for tile) + 25-word summary + 75–150 word description
   - 3 feature bullets tied to value (latency/cost/scale/security)
   - 2 targeted variants: SMB-focused & Enterprise-focused
4) Tech & integration checklist (owner: integration eng) [PASS/FAIL]
   - API endpoint / connector verified in dev (curl smoke test successful)
   - Auth model supported (OAuth2 client creds or marketplace token exchange)
   - Data residency option noted (if customer requires region pinning)
   - Minimum SLA/maintenance window documented for Dedicated / Private offers
5) Security & legal (owner: security/compliance) [PASS/FAIL]
   - Data handling statement (what we log/retain) present
   - PII / healthcare (HIPAA) flag raised if applicable
   - Standard indemnity/limits noted; any additional contract redlines flagged
6) Telemetry & billing signals (owner: SRE / listing ops) [PASS/FAIL]
   - Usage events (tokens, embeddings units) mapped to metering metrics
   - Error/latency counters and basic trace IDs available for tile support

Scoring rubric (for 72-hr fast track):
- Green: all must-pass items are PASS; start copy/design handoff
- Amber: 1 must-pass missing + plan with owner and ETA (<= 5 business days)
- Red: >1 must-pass missing or any legal/security open -> escalate to enterprise intake

Copy playbook: microcopy templates (editable)
- Tile headline (20 chars): "Low-latency LLM inference"
- 25-word summary: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost. Use Redwood-hosted inference or dedicated capacity for enterprise-grade SLAs and private deployments."
- 50-word summary (alternate): "Redwood Inference powers scalable LLM features: hosted APIs for fast integration, reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput, and private deploy options for regulated data. Fast onboarding, transparent pricing, and production observability included."

SMB-tailored variant (tone: approachable, outcome-focused):
- Headline: "Add LLM features without ops work"
- 25-word blurb: "Build search, summarization, and chat quickly with a pay-as-you-go API. No infra to manage — optimize cost with automatic batching and caching."

Enterprise-tailored variant (tone: control, compliance):
- Headline: "Predictable inference for critical apps"
- 25-word blurb: "Reserved GPU pools, VPC/private control plane, and audit logs for compliance. SLA-backed operations and support for KMS/HSM key management."

Feature bullets (3 examples to pick from and edit):
- "Low-latency inference at scale — optimized runtime and smart batching deliver consistent tail latencies."
- "Cost controls for unit economics — intelligent batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token spend."
- "Enterprise security — private deploys, VPC options, and KMS/HSM integrations with audit trails."

Legal/Compliance microcopy (for tile footnote):
- "Data processed for inference; logs retained for X days. See partner contract for DPA and Data Retention terms."
- If HIPAA/healthcare: "Not suitable for PHI without a signed BAA and deployment in Private mode. Contact security@redwood.ai."

Acceptance gating: minimal technical smoke tests (integration eng to run):
1) Auth: exchange marketplace token -> get bearer token (screenshot of curl response 200)
2) Basic inference: POST /v1/generate with short prompt -> response with tokens and latency <= expected threshold (capture headers trace-id)
3) Error path: invalid key -> returns 401 with helpful error message
4) Telemetry: event emitted to listing ingestion (billing.Counter increment) on each request

Launch ops runbook (abbreviated):
- Day -7: Final copy locked; legal sign-off for DPA/terms; assets uploaded to publisher portal
- Day -3: Tech smoke tests green; billing mapping in place; support playbook drafted
- Day 0: Publish tile; watch 4x hourly dashboards for first 48 hours; prepare rollback plan
- Day +7: Readout: conversion metrics, error rates, partner feedback

Telemetry event map (examples to include in listing metadata):
- marketplace.request.received -> {plan, region, model_variant}
- marketplace.request.succeeded -> {tokens, cost_units, latency_ms}
- marketplace.request.failed -> {error_code}

Common blockers and mitigations (from recent runs):
- Blocker: partner only supplies SAML SSO; mitigation: accept SAML for partner console but require marketplace token exchange for API access
- Blocker: partner expects long-term token retention; mitigation: define token TTL policy and justify for security/compliance
- Blocker: missing logo assets or wrong aspect ratio; mitigation: use placeholder splash + schedule asset replacement in 48 hrs

Unresolved questions (log here during intake):
- Does partner need dedicated encryption keys (HSM)? If yes, which cloud KMS provider?
- Are regional data residency controls required for EU/UK customers?
- Is the partner offering a managed private deployment (on-prem) or only hosted on Redwood?

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Draft 25/75-word copy variants (Alyssa) - ETA: 2025-11-08
- Run auth + inference smoke test (Evan) - ETA: 2025-11-07
- Upload assets to publisher portal and validate thumbnails (Listing Ops: Priya) - ETA: 2025-11-09
- Legal quick-check for DPA / HIPAA flag (Diego) - ETA: 2025-11-11

Sample outreach snippet to partner (email):
Subject: Marketplace tile: next steps and 72-hr fast-track
Hi <partner contact>,
Thanks for the call — attaching a short checklist we’ll use to fast-track the listing. Can you deliver the short blurb, logo (SVG), and confirm auth flow by EOD Thursday? If not, we’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up to resolve blocking items.
Thanks,
Alyssa (Redwood GTM)

Notes for listing ops (publishing quick checklist):
- Confirm publisher portal metadata fields are filled (contact, support URL, trial SKU)
- Ensure billing mappings to metering metrics are created and tested in sandbox
- Attach support playbook: escalation path, sample logs, trace-id guidance

Post-launch readout template (for 7-day):
- Traffic: requests/day, unique customers, conversion rate by trial->paid
- Ops: error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, top 3 errors and remediation status
- Business: revenue booked (if available), partner feedback summary

=================================
Appendix: copy snippets bank (quick grab-and-paste)
- "Get high-quality LLM outputs with minimal ops — API-first integration, pay-as-you-go, and built-in tooling to keep costs down."
- "Reserved GPU pools for steady throughput and low jitter — ideal for customer-facing production features."
- "Ship features quickly: prebuilt connectors, model suggestions, and automated batching to reduce token spend."

Last thoughts: keep the initial tile focused on value (what customers can do) rather than architecture. Reserve deep technical detail for the product page or linked docs. Use the rubric above to decide whether to do a 72-hr fast-track or a full enterprise intake.

-- end of mini-audit playbook (draft)
